text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

Abstract  
We queried the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) for Series accession GSE309890 to (i) summarise the study and (ii) list the downloadable data files. Using the geo_series tool, which wraps two E-utilities requests (esummary for metadata plus an FTP directory listing), we retrieved one GEO Series record (uid 200309890). The study investigates how the antidepressant sertraline biases antibiotic-resistance evolution in Escherichia coli K-12 by rewiring the pentose-phosphate pathway. It contains six RNA-seq samples (three controls and three 40-day sertraline-adapted cultures) on platform GPL24659. No PubMed article is presently linked. One compressed CSV matrix (510 KB) is available for download.

I. Introduction  
Background. Sertraline, a selective serotonin-reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), can modulate bacterial physiology and possibly accelerate antibiotic resistance. Understanding the metabolic basis of this effect in E. coli has clinical relevance.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The processed data files and study details for GSE309890 had not been enumerated.  
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: retrieve the study synopsis and catalogue all supplementary files. Hypothesis: GEO lists at least one processed expression matrix downloadable from its FTP site.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. Query GEO for Series GSE309890, then list its supplementary files.  
Materials. NCBI GEO via geo_series (entrez esummary + FTP).  
Procedures.  
1. geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)  
   • Internally issues esummary (db=gds, id=200309890) to obtain metadata.  
   • Crawls FTP path https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/ for file list.  
Statistical Analysis. Counts are direct from returned arrays (sample_count, supplementary_files length).

III. Results  
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. Key attributes of GEO Series GSE309890  

| Field | Value | Source |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Accession | GSE309890 | esummary |
| Title | “Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback” | esummary |
| Organism | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | esummary |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | esummary |
| Samples (n) | 6 (3 controls, 3 adapted) | esummary |
| Platform | GPL24659 | esummary |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 | esummary |
| PubMed links | None registered | esummary |
| Supplementary files (n) | 1 | FTP listing |

Table 2. Downloadable supplementary file(s) for GSE309890  

| File name | Size | URL |
|-----------|------|-----|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510 KB | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz |

Findings. The Series contains RNA-seq data comparing sertraline-adapted versus control E. coli populations. One processed expression matrix (FPKM values for all six samples) is downloadable from the GEO FTP ‘suppl’ directory.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The study focuses on metabolic adaptations (notably transketolase A involvement in the PPP) that confer antibiotic-resistance advantages after chronic sertraline exposure. The single CSV.gz file likely holds gene-level FPKM quantifications needed for downstream differential-expression analyses.  
Context. Absence of a PubMed link suggests the manuscript is unpublished or not yet indexed; nonetheless, data are publicly available.  
Limitations. GEO metadata do not confirm raw FASTQ availability; only processed counts were returned. Additional raw sequencing data may reside in SRA BioProject PRJNA1363958, which was not queried here.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 provides a concise six-sample RNA-seq dataset exploring SSRI-induced resistance mechanisms. Future work should (i) retrieve raw reads from PRJNA1363958 for independent re-analysis and (ii) perform differential-expression and pathway enrichment focusing on PPP and redox-related genes.

References  
[1] NCBI GEO Series GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO FTP directory for GSE309890 supplementary files. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/  
[3] NCBI E-utilities esummary call (GSE309890). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0  

Acknowledgments  
We thank the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus team for providing open access to transcriptomic datasets and associated metadata.
